title: world.counters gpu reports the world engine's counted work for its newest completed submission, pass by pass in order, identically on both backends
binding: The positive leg boots a still offscreen world with one SDF view, waits for the engine to be ready (world.wait ready: its pipeline set installed and its first frame produced), and reads the gpu section of world.counters sixty completed ticks later and again after thirty more. The world node's line in each response carries its submission, and the second read's is greater: a later submission. The world node's ten pass lines appear in pass order: upload executes nothing, because the device's memory profile selects the ring policy for every table the engine writes (a host-visible aperture, which this canary's reference machine reports on both backends), so the kernels read the ring slot's own buffer and nothing is copied, and the work outside every pass writes the one word of the viewport row the frame's presentation time moved, 4 bytes, the only host-visible write a still frame makes (a device whose profile selects the staged policy instead records one copy and one transition in upload, and a header and run entry beside the word); sky through views read skipped because the cadence gate re-composites the still frame, and composite executes its one indirect dispatch; the work outside every pass and the node's created objects follow, with no pipeline or shader module among them, because the shared SDF pipeline cache creates and counts those under gpu.sdf-pipelines. The exact lines hold on Vulkan and Direct3D 12 alike, which is the cross-backend proof. The discriminating leg reads world.counters gpu twice before the first tick, when no submission has completed, so neither read shows a pass line and the positive's exact lines turn red.
